> Any idea for a next step?

yes, the best option is to get the latest Psalm `dev-master` where I've added a `--debug-by-line` option, allowing you to identify the particular line Psalm fails on.

Also, sorry you found this bug!

**Edit**: Disregard, solved with `composer update`.
Then it would be `composer require --dev --update-with-all-dependencies vimeo/psalm:dev-master`

Now that's totally different problem, related to fresh from-the-oven callable syntax additions.
/ping @muglug
Is there any specific construct in the code-base that triggers this error?

The reference to `register_shutdown_function()` in this case. However it's quite possible that other built-in functions are currently affected. Psalm apparently not yet fully compatible with the function map imported from Phan.

If your `vendor/vimeo/psalm` (assuming standard composer layout) contains a git checkout, you may try to go back before the commit that imported that map (`git checkout 3ef70738623af08ef2624ac522e9ddf3c83e220e^` should do the trick, caret is important here).
Again, running with `--debug-by-line` will tell you where Psalm is failing
@olleharstedt @weirdan yes, sorry those were broken by changes made last night. Latest `dev-master` should protect against those issues.
And parsing of `callable() : void` is also fixed now, in case you were dying to use that
